The resulting dam collapse released some 14.4 billion cubic meters of water, ooding downstream environments and ushing unknown quantities of debris, pollutants and sediments into the north-western Black Sea. With a combined satellite and hydrological modelling approach, supported with in situ data, we assessed the short-term impact on the north-western Black Sea. Thedam breach impacted more than 50% of the area of the north-western Black Sea, experiencing over 50times the ambient Chlorophyll- aand suspended sediment concentrations. Signi cant increases of nitrate and phosphate were also observed in the Odesa coastal environment. This environmentalshock triggered severe algal blooms within one week, that persisted for a further 20 days. This eventmay have impacted the biodiversity of the north-western Black Sea and its ecosystem response.

nodes.question: What caused eutrophication in the Black Sea?
nodes.answer: Eutrophication in the Black Sea was caused by excessive loading of nutrients, leading to phytoplankton blooms and expanded hypoxia and anoxia zones.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the Ebro Delta influence nutrient availability in the study area?
nodes.answer: The Ebro Delta receives high riverine inputs from the Ebro River and the Rhone River, which contribute to nutrient availability in the area, assisted by local upwelling events.
nodes.paragraph: 2014; Bevilacqua et al. 2019; Chakravorty et al. 2024). Materials and methods Study area The study area is the surroundings of the Ebro Delta, in the Northwestern Mediterranean Sea, from Vilanova i la Geltr , in the north, to Castell de la Plana, in the south, covering approximately 8,0 km2 and including part of the coastal area, continental shelf, and upper slope (35 400 m) (Fig. 1). Despite that the Mediterranean Sea is generally considered oligotrophic, this area receives high riverine inputs from the Ebro river (Estrada 1996) and from the Rhone River in the north (France), which are transported southwestwards along the continental slope by the Liguro-Proven al-Catalan cur - rent (Estrada 1996). In addition, local upwelling events (i.e., eddies) also enhance nutrient availability. The area is also characterized by strong seasonality (Vilas et al. 2020; Lloret- Lloret et al. 2021).
